rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection property (unformalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever T ⊢ σ then AE ⊢ Prb_T(σ); and if T includes AE then T has re�a7ection: T ⊢ σ implies T ⊢ Prb_T(σ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (a) is immediate from the representability of the deduction relation; part (b) follows because AE proves the representation, so if AE ⊆ T, T inherits the fact that proofs imply provability-statements. Note: this is not the same as T proving (σ → Prb_T(σ)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'suf�a7ciently strong' theory (three derivability conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Call T 'suf�a7ciently strong' if it meets the following three formalized derivability conditions: (1) AE ⊆ T. (2) For any sentence σ, T ⊢ (Prb_T(σ) → Prb_T(Prb_T(σ))). (3) For any sentences ρ and σ, T ⊢ (Prb_T(ρ → σ) → (Prb_T(ρ) → Prb_T(σ))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the standard Hilbert-Bernays-L�f6b derivability conditions presented as requirements to carry out the formalized parts of the second incompleteness argument inside T. Condition (1) guarantees (unformalized) reflection; (2) is formalized reflection; (3) is formalized modus ponens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalized Lemma 37B (formal consequence used in proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T is a suf�a7ciently strong recursively axiomatizable theory and let σ be such that AE ⊢ (σ ↔ �not Prb_T(σ)). Then T ⊢ (Cons(T) → �not Prb_T(σ)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formalized step that, together with the rest of the derivability conditions, yields G�f6del's second theorem. It shows how, inside T, provability of Cons(T) leads to inconsistency unless T is inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Cons(T) used in the text
rubrics_metrics.description: Cons(T) is the sentence ¬ Prb_T(0 = S0), thought of as saying 'T is consistent' (here 0 = S0 is chosen as a convenient refutable sentence in AE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a fixed false arithmetic sentence as the canonical contradiction lets one formalize 'no proof of contradiction' as ¬Prb_T(0 = S0). This specific choice is used in the formalized derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: G�f6del's Second Incompleteness Theorem (sufficient condition form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T is a suf�a7ciently strong recursively axiomatizable theory. Then T ⊢ Cons(T) iff T is inconsistent (equivalently: if T ⊢ Cons(T) then T is inconsistent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central conclusion: a sufficiently strong recursively axiomatizable consistent theory cannot prove its own consistency. The three derivability conditions above are the sufficient hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: L�f6b's theorem condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a suf�a7ciently strong recursively axiomatizable theory and τ is any sentence for which T ⊢ (Prb_T(τ) → τ), then T ⊢ τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem is proved by constructing σ that says 'if I am provable then τ' (fixed-point lemma) and applying Formalized Lemma 37C. This shows the equivalence T ⊢ (Prb_T(τ) → τ) ⇔ T ⊢ τ in such theories and is used to deduce the second incompleteness theorem by taking τ to be 0 = S0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation π: demands for embedding Cn(AE) into ST
rubrics_metrics.description: To interpret Cn(AE) into a set theory ST one must produce formulas π_∀, π_0, π_S, π_<, π_+, π_·, π_E etc. so that (i) ∃v1 π_∀ is in ST; (ii) for each function symbol f of AE, ST contains a sentence asserting π_f defines a function on the set defined by π_∀ (uniqueness/existence and closure properties); (iii) for each of the 11 base sentences σ in AE, the translated sentence σ^π is in ST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These (finite) demands ensure π is an interpretation of AE into ST. The text sketches standard constructions (e.g., represent natural numbers by Von Neumann ordinals, define successor, addition via recursion on ω, etc.). The finiteness of requirements allows finding a finite subset of ST witnessing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong undecidability of set theory (Theorem 37D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T be a theory in the language of set theory such that T ∪ ST (or at least T ∪ some finite subset witnessing the interpretation) is consistent. Then Th(T) is not recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces nonrecursiveness of an arithmetical fragment (pulled back via the interpretation) to nonrecursiveness of T. The lemma that the mapping α ↦ α^π on G�f6del numbers is recursive is used to effect the many-one reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 37E: recursive translation function p
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a recursive function p such that for any formula α of the language of number theory, p(⎡α⎤) = ⎡α^π⎤ (the G�f6del number of the translation under π).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the effective computability of the translation operation on G�f6del numbers and is crucial to many-one reducibility arguments used in undecidability proofs. The construction follows the explicit syntactic procedures of Section 2.7 and the encodings in Sections 3.3–3.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of a G�f6del-type sentence for ST (Lemma 37H requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a sentence σ of number theory whose translation σ^π asserts 'σ^π is not a theorem of ST' (constructed using a recursive ternary relation D(a,b,c) that holds iff a is the G�f6del number of a formula α and c is the number of a deduction in ST of α(Sb0)^π). If ST is consistent then σ^π ∉ ST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the usual diagonal construction adapted to the interpretation into set theory; the lemma demonstrates the analogue of the G�f6del sentence for ST and underlies the second incompleteness theorem for ST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of exponentiation in Cn(AM) (Lemma 38A / Theorem 38C)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a function δ representable in Cn(AM) such that for every finite sequence a_0,...,a_n there is an s with δ(s,i) = a_i for all i ≤ n; using such a δ one can define E**(a,b) = least s with δ(s,0) = 1 and for all i < b, δ(s,i+1) = δ(s,i) · a, and then ab = δ(E**(a,b), b). Hence exponentiation is representable in Cn(AM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The key is to produce a sequence-encoding/decoding function δ in the language without exponentiation. The construction uses a pairing function J and the G�f6del β-function; existence of suitable c,d for Chinese remainder congruences guarantees the encoding. This shows that adding multiplication (but not E) suffices to represent E primitively in AM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairing function J and projections K,L representability
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a standard pairing function J(a,b) = 1/2(a+b)(a+b+1) + a with projections K and L giving the coordinates: K(J(a,b)) = a and L(J(a,b)) = b. These functions (and an auxiliary H) are representable in Cn(AM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives an explicit arithmetic formula and reductions showing J,K,L (and H, the halving-like function) are definable/representable in AM; these are used to combine c and d into a single code J(c,d) so that δ(J(c,d),i) = β(c,d,i).

rubrics_metrics.name: G�f6del -function (β) and Chinese Remainder conditions (Lemma 38B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define β(c,d,i) as the remainder in c ÷ [1 + (i+1)·d] (the least r with c = q·[1+(i+1)d] + r). Choosing d = s! for s large enough makes the moduli 1+(i+1)d pairwise relatively prime (Lemma 38B), so by the Chinese Remainder Theorem one can find c giving prescribed remainders a_i for i ≤ n; thus δ(s,i) := β(K(s),L(s),i) satisfies the sequence-coding property required in Lemma 38A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presents the concrete arithmetic criterion used to guarantee existence of a code c with specified sequence of residues: take moduli 1+(i+1)s! which are pairwise coprime, then apply CRT. Lemma 38B proves pairwise coprimality; CRT yields c.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim: Any recursive relation is representable in Cn(AM)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the constructions above (representability results for basic arithmetic operations, pairing, β-function, and sequence coding), any recursive relation is representable in Cn(AM), and any recursive function is functionally representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the summary conclusion: the representability proofs of Sections 3.3–3.5 (with exponentiation replaced by its AM-representation) show that NM/AM suffice to represent all recursive relations. Consequently, theories T in the language of NM with T ∪ AM consistent are strongly undecidable.
